chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has made the sustenance of the believers come from where they do not expect, and that is because when the servant does not know the source of his sustenance, his supplication increases.

key_terms.أَرْزَاقَ: provisions or sustenances allotted by Allah
key_terms.الْعَبْدَ: the servant, meaning the human being in relation to Allah
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the believers, those characterized by iman
key_terms.تَبَارَكَ وَ تَعَالَى: Blessed and Exalted, a formula affirming Allah's majesty and transcendence
key_terms.مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُونَ: from where they do not expect or anticipate
key_terms.وَجْهَ رِزْقِهِ: the source or direction of his sustenance

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah provide believers from where they do not expect?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, provides for the believers from unexpected avenues. It explains that when a servant does not know exactly from where his provision will come, he turns more often to du'a, increasing his dependence upon Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "Indeed, Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, has made the sustenance of the believers come from where they do not expect. This is because when a servant does not know the source of his sustenance, his supplications increase."
